title: CITIZEN'S ARREST: Vaporize blocks legacy products with no working path to legitimacy - the InternationalLawBaseline ratchet exists but the preflight never reads it
description: Filed at the owning home, citizen's-arrest style. Observed 2026-08-25 while dispatching the swift-windows-ui hello-world demo through 'vaporize run swift-win' on Windows: the i18n source gate correctly blocked dispatch (I18N001/I18N002, four typed beads auto-filed with spawn casts - the gate itself worked beautifully). But then the flow dead-ends. The ONLY sanctioned relief valve, InternationalLawBaseline (TranslateCatalogCore/Sources/TranslateSourceGate/InternationalLawBaseline.swift), is fully implemented - formatVersion 0.1.0, binding identity, scannedFiles completeness guard, structural-anchor entries, ratchet semantics 'a ratchet not a waiver' - and referenced by NOTHING. I18nSourceGatePreflight.swift does not consume it. There is no CLI flag, no baseline-capture command, no documented flow that says: gate blocks legacy product -> freeze pre-existing findings as baseline -> dispatch succeeds -> ratchet prevents regression. Instructions are unclear to the point of absent. An operator holding a legitimate legacy product and a working gate has no documented path from one to the other. RESOLUTION 2026-08-25 (liberated): Proven by:
acceptanceCriteria: I18nSourceGatePreflight consumes InternationalLawBaseline: pre-existing structural-anchor findings frozen at baseline pass; any newly observed finding still fails. A baseline capture surface exists (CLI mode or documented file contract) with the binding identity preventing cross-boundary reuse. The flow gate-block -> baseline-freeze -> dispatch is documented where the gate error message points, so the next operator is not left holding a block with no lever. The swift-windows-ui hello-world demo dispatches through vaporize after its pre-existing findings are baselined, and any newly introduced string fails as the ratchet demands.
